messages.accueilMessage:
The Hydrology Observatory Database (Base de Données des Observatoires en Hydrologie, BDOH) aims at managing, banking and providing hydrological and biochemical data from long-term observatories managed by or where Irstea (formerly Cemagref) is strongly involved. These observatories consist of experimental sites in which data are collected continuously or during recurring campaigns: rainfall, water height and river flow rates, groundwater levels, suspended matter flow, concentration of various substances, etc. The oldest observatory has been operating since 1962.

Those data are used for research by scientists of Irstea and their partners, as well as the public or private operational community for environment (State services, territory authorities, design offices, industry). The data are accessible to everyone as long as the users register on the application and observe the terms of uses.

In BDOH, data are naturally organised by Observatories, which are independently managed by the research units in charge.

messages.measure.export.help-content:
• The time zone for the selection of start/end dates and hours is UTC.
  • The default option for download is "identical time step":
    • the original time step of the time series is conserved (it is potentially variable)
    • several time series belonging to a same station can be downloaded at the same time
    • the file is directly downloaded from BDOH without any size restriction.
  • Some time series can be downloaded with an option for fixed time step calculation (using linear interpolation, mean calculation or sum calculation):
    • only one time series can be downloaded at a time
    • in order not to block the server, each download is limited to a maximum span of 2 years per minute of time step, i.e. 1051200 values (~ 106 lines)
    • if a calculation is needed on a longer span, the download must be performed onto a series of smaller spans
    • data are sent by e-mail as attached file
    • the options for fiexed time step calculation are: (i) for linear interpolation, a time step between 1 and 1440 minutes; (ii) for mean and sum calculations, one of the time steps available in the drop-down list. The interpolated values start at a round time. Option “ event ” calculates the mean or sum of the values in the time range of the event (1 output value).
  • One separate file is downloaded for each time series.
  • For downloads of continuous time series with identical time step or linear interpolation, several file formats are available (BDOH standard or Hydro2 QTVAR).
  • For fix time steps with mean/sum calculation options, the only possible file format is "BDOH discontinu".

messages.measure.import.formats.Bdoh:
• Header (3 lines):
    • "Station ; Fuseau ; Followed by, for N time series: Chronique ; Unite ; Chronique ; Unite ... (N times)"
    • "station code ; timezone value (format: UTC +/-HH) ; time series code 1 ; time series unit 1 ; time series code 2 ; time series unit 2 ... (N times)"
    • "DateHeure ; Valeur ; Qualite ; Min (optional) ; Max (optional) ; Valeur ; Qualite ; Min (optional) ; Max (optional) ... (N times)"
  • Data: "DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS ; value ; quality code ; value (optional) ; value (optional) ; value ; quality code ; value (optional) ; value (optional) ... (N times)"
  • Special values and missing values:
    • -9999 for gap values;
    • The quality code must match the quality set used by the observatory.
  • Comments:
    • The character '#' indicates a comment line and can also be found inside the line, in which case the rest of the line is ignored;
    • Comments are not allowed in the first three lines of the file, which must always be the header as described here.
  • Min and max columns go compulsorily together but they may be present or not depending of each time series.
messages.measure.import.formats.BdohPlage:
• Header (3 lines):
    • "Station ; Fuseau ; Followed by, for N time series: Chronique ; Unite ; Chronique ; Unite ... (N times)"
    • "station code ; timezone value (format: UTC +/-HH) ; time series code 1 ; time series unit 1 ; time series code 2 ; time series unit 2 ... (N times)"
    • "Debut ; Fin ; Valeur ; Qualite ; Min (optional) ; Max (optional) ; Valeur ; Qualite ; Min (optional) ; Max (optional) ... (N times)"
  • Data: "DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS ; DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS ; value ; quality code ; value (optional) ; value (optional) ; value ; quality code ; value (optional) ; value (optional) ... (N times)"
  • Special values and missing values:
    • -9999 for gap values;
    • The quality code must match the quality set used by the observatory.
  • Comments:
    • The character '#' indicates a comment line and can also be found inside the line, in which case the rest of the line is ignored;
    • Comments are not allowed in the first three lines of the file, which must always be the header as described here.
  • Min and max columns go compulsorily together but they may be present or not depending of each time series.
messages.measure.import.formats.Qjo:
• Header (3 lines): Not used
  • Data: "QJ0 ; HYDRO2 staion code (not used) ; YYYYMMDD ; value (in l/s) ; C or S ; validity code ;"
  • Warning: Do not forget the last line which should look like "FIN;EXP-HYDRO;8007;"
messages.measure.import.formats.Qtvar:
• Header (4 lines): Not used
  • Data: "920 ; index (not used) ; HYDRO2 staion code (not used) ; YYYYMMDD ; HH:MM ; value (in m3/s) ; validity code ; continuity code ;"
  • Warning: Do not forget the last line which should look like "FIN;EXP-HYDRO;8007;"
messages.measure.import.formats.GrenobleDom:
• Header (1 line):
    • At least four fields separated by “ ; ”;
    • The station code is expected to be in the fourth field, the rest of the line is not used.
  • Data:
    • "DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS ; value ; quality ; comment";
    • The line mays also have extra “ ; ” after the comment.
  • Special values and missing values:
    • -999 for gap values;
    • The comment mays be empty or be “ ras ”, it is not used;
    • The quality code must match the quality set Draix which must also be the one used by the observatory.

messages.shape.import.format.coursEau:
• One zipped file with the same name as all the files inside, without folders.
  • Expected attribute columns, without specific order (based on the Carthage format):
    • toponyme, for the name of the river;
    • code_hydro, for the hydro code of the river, can be empty, the code must be a string;
    • classifica, for the Strahler number of the river, can be empty, must be a number.

messages.colors.default.qualite:
For the simple-viewer, the initial values are: color #FF0000 (red) and thickness 5 for the qualities processed as a gap and color #0000FF (blue) and thickness 1 for the other qualities.
For information: For the multi-viewer, one color is generated automatically and used for the whole time series (including gap qualities that are displayed with a transparency effect). Line thickness is 5 for the gap qualities and 1 for the others. These styles cannot be changed.
messages.colors.default.discontinuous:
For the simple-viewer, the initial values are: shape ●, thickness 2 and size 5.
For information: For the multi-viewer the following values are used: shape ●, thickness 2 and size 5. This style cannot be changed.
messages.colors.default.checkpoint:
For the simple-viewer, the initial values are: shape ○, thickness 2, color #008000 (green) and size 5.
For information: Checkpoints are not displayed on the multi-viewer.
